text:
Liam (Customer): Hey, running into a nasty failure with tool calling when we try to invoke two tools in parallel. The model response sometimes attributes the result from tool A to tool B. Example: we call `geo_lookup` and `kb_search` at the same time but the `kb_search` result shows up under `geo_lookup` in the final output. request id 20260315-rlw-0123.

Asha (Support): Sorry you're hitting this, Liam. Can you paste the exact request payload (sanitized) and a snippet of the response you're seeing? Also which Redwood model/runtime are you using?

Liam (Customer): Sure. Using hosted API `redwood-l2.1` via the function-calling interface. Payload (redacted):

```json
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-l2.1",
  "input": "Find coordinates and docs for company X",
  "tools": [
    {"name": "geo_lookup", "schema": {"lat": "number","lon": "number"}},
    {"name": "kb_search", "schema": {"id": "string","snippet": "string"}}
  ],
  "tool_calling": {"mode": "parallel"},
  "debug": true
}
```

Response we get (trimmed):
```json
{
  "id": "20260315-rlw-0123",
  "choices": [
    {
      "tool_calls": [
        {"name": "geo_lookup", "args": {"q": "company X"}, "result": {"id": "doc-435","snippet":"An engineering office in SF"}},
        {"name": "kb_search", "args": {"q": "company X"}, "result": {"lat": 37.78, "lon": -122.41}}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

So the `geo_lookup` tool shows a KB snippet and `kb_search` returns coordinates. Looks like results and tools are swapped. Happens sporadically.

Asha (Support): ugh. OK. Noted. @Priya can you weigh in on whether we've seen mis-association in parallel tool runs?

Priya (Eng-ML): I haven't seen this exact symptom in unit tests, but this smells like a race/association bug in the code that stitches tool_results back to the model's tool_calls when multiple tools are executing concurrently. Two quick hypotheses: (1) tool_result mapping uses positional indexing and a non-deterministic ordering of async completions flips things; (2) the model itself emitted tool_call messages in a different order than we scheduled tool runs, and we match by position.

Jared (SRE): Can you also paste the per-request debug log we produce when `debug=true`? That includes the call trace and the per-tool correlation ids. If you don't have logs, ask your infra folks to share the full response headers and the raw `x-redwood-trace` header.

Liam (Customer): I have the debug log. Pasting the relevant bits (sanitized):

```
[2026-03-15T14:12:05Z] root: received generate request id=20260315-rlw-0123
[2026-03-15T14:12:05Z] tool-orchestrator: scheduled tool geo_lookup call id=call_7a
[2026-03-15T14:12:05Z] tool-orchestrator: scheduled tool kb_search call id=call_b3
[2026-03-15T14:12:06Z] tool-geo_lookup: started call call_7a
[2026-03-15T14:12:06Z] tool-kb_search: started call call_b3
[2026-03-15T14:12:07Z] tool-kb_search: success call_b3 -> result_id=res_b3
[2026-03-15T14:12:07Z] tool-geo_lookup: success call_7a -> result_id=res_7a
[2026-03-15T14:12:07Z] stitcher: mapping tool_calls -> results by index [0->res_b3, 1->res_7a]
[2026-03-15T14:12:07Z] stitcher: final choice.tool_calls[0].result = res_b3
```

So the stitcher mapped by the order of completion (res_b3 finished first) rather than the tool identity.

Priya (Eng-ML): That confirms hypothesis (1). We should be matching by a stable call id (call_7a/call_b3) or by tool name emitted by the model, not by completion order. Thanks for the logs.

Asha (Support): Workaround for now: please force `tool_calling.mode = sequential` or add a short `concurrency: 1` in your client to avoid parallel runs. That should prevent mis-association until we patch. Can you try and confirm?

Liam (Customer): I can try sequential mode — that'll cost a bit more latency but should be fine short-term. Will report back in ~30m.

Jared (SRE): We're going to escalate to eng-runtime to get a hotfix. @eng-runtime — can you prioritize a fix that uses call_id/tool_name to associate results, not positional indices? Also add a temporary guard in the stitcher so it logs a WARN if completion-order mapping differs from tool-name mapping.

eng-runtime: Thanks for the ping. We're on it. Initial triage: the stitcher code path `stitcher.v2` currently receives a list of tool_calls from the model and a list of tool_results from async executors. The historical approach has been to assume preservation of order, but with parallel async workers that assumption is brittle. We'll: (a) emit a correlation token (call_id) from orchestrator into the model-visible tool_call metadata, (b) match tool_results by call_id first, fallback to name+args hashes, and (c) add an integration test that runs 1000 randomized parallel tool calls to validate.

Priya (Eng-ML): Also adding a small change: require tools to include a `client_call_id` field in the args that we echo back; that'll make customer-side correlation trivial. Will include docs for this.

Asha (Support): TL;DR for the customer: switch to sequential mode or set concurrency=1 to avoid the symptom. We'll release a patch in the next dev cycle that properly matches results to calls. We'll also push a debug endpoint to re-run your request with instrumentation if you want us to reproduce it on our side.

Liam (Customer): Sequential confirmed — the swap no longer happens. Thanks. Please keep me posted on the patch timeline and whether you need my request logs for repro.

Jared (SRE): Patch plan: hotfix branch `stitcher/associations-202603` with the matching logic change, CI tests, and a canary deploy to staging within 48 hours. If staging looks good we'll roll to hosted API with a gradual traffic ramp (5%, 25%, 100%). We'll post updates to this thread and ping if we need the original traces.

eng-runtime: Assigned to @Priya and @Jared. We'll update status here. For now, short-term mitigation is documented and support will notify affected customers. :eyes:

support-bot: Incident created INC-2026-03-15-68 -> Severity: High (customer-visible incorrect results). Linked to ticket 5489.

Asha (Support): Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with Liam once PR is merged to staging. Liam — feel free to DM me the raw headers if you don't want them posted here.

Liam (Customer): Will do. Appreciate the rapid response! :heart:
